parts.display_text:
An object of mass m moves at speed u along a frictionless horizontal surface and collides head-on with a stationary object of mass 4m. After the collision, the object of mass m rebounds with speed u/2.

What is the speed of the object of mass 4m after the collision?

A. u/8
B. 3u/16
C. 5u/16
D. 3u/8

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: An object travels in a circle at constant speed. Name two vector quantities that change during the motion and explain why.

answer.text: Velocity and acceleration change because their directions change continuously. Velocity is tangential; acceleration points towards the centre. Momentum and the resultant force are also valid examples.

evidence.question: 5a
evidence.review: Worked answer checked against the source marking guidance; wording adapted for independent IB practice.

duplicate-4dec9a6f5005cda3.hint: Resolve forces parallel and perpendicular to the contact surface. Decide which way the object would tend to move.
notes: For a simple incline, weight has components mg sin θ down the plane and mg cos θ into it. Other applied forces can change the normal reaction.
Kinetic friction has magnitude μ_k N. Static friction adjusts up to μ_s N; use the maximum only at impending slip, and choose its direction to oppose relative slipping.

fep-0173f6e17d4c6961-q11:whole.hint: Choose the object or system and identify the resultant force, rather than using one force on its own.
notes: Newton’s second law is ΣF = ma. Resolve into independent directions; zero acceleration requires zero resultant force in that direction.
Newton’s third-law forces act on different bodies and are the same kind of interaction. Balanced forces act on the same body.
